question: After P0603 found tidal anisotropy and orientation weak, can the simpler conservative inward Green kernel find a universal galaxy-cluster balance?

simplified_operator.kernel: isotropic Gaussian centered L_i inward from each baryonic source
simplified_operator.mixture: route fraction=f_max*G(C)*S4; S4 is set to one only for normalized cluster morphology where physical acceleration is unavailable
simplified_operator.reason: their P0603 cluster response was small or adverse, while length, width, and fraction dominated

validation.selection: within each cluster fold choose minimum training Lenstool equal-cluster JS among candidates whose all-galaxy equal RMSE satisfies the fixed-RAR budget
validation.heldout: two complete clusters per fold; GLAFIC remains a method control not used in selection
validation.data_status: all galaxy and cluster data are spent; the exercise maps cross-domain parameter response rather than confirming a formula

claim_limits: All cluster targets and galaxy curves are spent data; whole-object folds do not make this a fresh confirmation.
Cluster maps use member light without a matched gas map and are lens-model reconstructions.
The galaxy test is an axisymmetric radial projection of the same conservative kernel.
The Solar result is an acceleration-screened uniform-Sun proxy, not a PPN derivation.
A balanced candidate must still be frozen and tested on raw lensing from another cluster.
